problems.quote: basaltic tuff from the Toba eruption
problems.problem: The volcanic ash layers at Bori are not from the Toba eruption (which occurred ~74,000 years ago); they are from a local volcanic event dated to ~670,000 years ago.
problems.correction: basaltic tuff from a local volcanic eruption
problems.verifierReason: Bori ash is from local ~670kya eruption, not Toba; correction accurate.

problems.quote: dated by radiocarbon to c. 25,000 BCE
problems.problem: Radiocarbon dates are reported in years BP (before present), not BCE. The Patne ostrich eggshell is radiocarbon dated to ~25,000 BP, which calibrates to ~23,000 BCE.
problems.correction: radiocarbon dated to c. 25,000 BP
problems.verifierReason: Radiocarbon dates reported in BP, not BCE; correction proper.

problems.quote: Elephas hysudrindicus
problems.problem: The species name is misspelled; the correct spelling is Elephas hysudricus.
problems.correction: Elephas hysudricus
problems.verifierReason: Species name misspelled; correct spelling is Elephas hysudricus.

problems.quote: Preventive detention — extended for 3 months without advisory board (otherwise must get board approval)
problems.problem: Incorrectly states that preventive detention can be extended for 3 months without an advisory board; actually detention up to 3 months is allowed without board, but extension beyond 3 months requires advisory board approval.
problems.correction: Preventive detention up to 3 months without advisory board; beyond that requires board approval
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates Art 22(4): detention up to 3 months allowed without board; extension beyond requires board. Correction is precise.

problems.quote: Art 46 — promote educational/economic interests of SC/ST/OBC
problems.problem: Article 46 refers to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and weaker sections; it does not specifically mention OBC.
problems.correction: Art 46 — promote educational/economic interests of SC/ST and weaker sections
problems.verifierReason: Art 46 mentions SC/ST and weaker sections, not OBC. Correction accurately reflects constitutional text.

problems.quote: The Parliament may, by a resolution supported by not less than 2/3 of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha, create one or more All India Services
problems.problem: All India Services are created by a law passed by Parliament under Article 312, not by a Rajya Sabha resolution.
problems.correction: Parliament may, by a law passed under Article 312, create All India Services
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates procedure; correction correctly states creation by law under Art 312.

problems.quote: He defeated the local king of Taxila, Ambhi (Omphis) , who submitted without a fight
problems.problem: Ambhi submitted without a fight; he was not defeated in battle.
problems.correction: He received the submission of the local king of Taxila, Ambhi (Omphis), who surrendered without a fight
problems.verifierReason: Original says 'defeated' but Ambhi submitted without battle; correction accurately states 'received submission'.

problems.quote: Chandragupta Maurya conquered the Punjab from the Greek satrap Seleucus Nicator in 305 BCE
problems.problem: Seleucus Nicator was a king, not a satrap; the Punjab was taken from Greek satraps earlier (c. 317 BCE).
problems.correction: Chandragupta Maurya took the Punjab from Greek satraps by 317 BCE and later made a treaty with Seleucus Nicator in 305 BCE
problems.verifierReason: Seleucus was a king, not satrap; Punjab taken earlier from Greek satraps. Correction fixes both errors.

problems.quote: EAST: Magadha, Anga, Vrijji, Malla, Shakya
problems.problem: Shakya is not one of the 16 Mahajanapadas; the standard list includes 16 without Shakya.
problems.correction: EAST: Magadha, Anga, Vrijji, Malla
problems.verifierReason: Shakya is not among the 16 Mahajanapadas; standard list excludes it. Correction removes Shakya.

problems.quote: India is the world's largest producer and exporter of mica , accounting for about 60% of global production.
problems.problem: India is not the world's largest producer of mica overall; China is. India is the largest producer of sheet mica.
problems.correction: India is the world's largest producer and exporter of sheet mica, accounting for about 60% of global sheet mica production.
problems.verifierReason: Original incorrectly states India is largest mica producer overall; China leads in total mica. Correction accurately specifies sheet mica.

problems.quote: operating 10 of India's 23 refineries
problems.problem: Indian Oil Corporation operates 9 refineries, not 10.
problems.correction: operating 9 of India's 23 refineries
problems.verifierReason: IOC operates 9 refineries, not 10. Correction matches current official count.

problems.quote: Chandikhol (0.75 MT, Odisha, rock cavern Phase II, completed 2024)
problems.problem: Chandikhol SPR capacity is 4 MT, not 0.75 MT, and it is not completed as of 2024.
problems.correction: Chandikhol (4 MT, Odisha, rock cavern Phase II, under construction)
problems.verifierReason: Chandikhol SPR capacity is 4 MT (not 0.75 MT) and remains under construction as of 2024.

problems.quote: India has about 500,000 tonnes of monazite (the primary thorium-bearing mineral), the largest in the world
problems.problem: India's monazite reserves are about 12 million tonnes, not 500,000 tonnes.
problems.correction: India has about 12 million tonnes of monazite (the primary thorium-bearing mineral), the largest in the world
problems.verifierReason: India's monazite resources are ~12 million tonnes per AMD, not 500,000 tonnes.

problems.quote: The ISA is the first international organisation headquartered in India and is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation under the UN.
problems.problem: ISA is not under the UN; it is an independent treaty-based intergovernmental organisation.
problems.correction: The ISA is the first international organisation headquartered in India and is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation.
problems.verifierReason: ISA is an independent treaty-based organisation, not 'under the UN'. Correction removes inaccurate phrase.

problems.quote: Monitors safeguards for religious and linguistic minorities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis).
problems.problem: NCM monitors only religious minorities; linguistic minorities are handled by a separate Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
problems.correction: Monitors safeguards for religious minorities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis).
problems.verifierReason: NCM monitors only religious minorities; linguistic minorities handled by separate Commissioner under Art. 350B. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: The Rajya Sabha has equal representation for all States (not proportional to population), protecting smaller States.
problems.problem: Rajya Sabha seats are allocated roughly in proportion to state population, not equally. Equal representation is a feature of the US Senate.
problems.correction: The Rajya Sabha represents States in proportion to population, not equally.
problems.verifierReason: Rajya Sabha seats allocated roughly by population, not equally. Correction correctly states proportional representation.

problems.quote: Unlike the USA and Australia (where there is dual citizenship — of the Union and of the individual State)
problems.problem: Australia has a single national citizenship; there is no separate state citizenship. Only the USA has a form of dual citizenship (national and state).
problems.correction: Unlike the USA (where there is dual citizenship — of the Union and of the individual State)
problems.verifierReason: Australia has single citizenship; only USA has dual citizenship (federal/state). Correction removes erroneous Australia reference.

problems.quote: 50M hectares of degraded land by 2030 (UNCCD target)
problems.problem: India's UNCCD land restoration target is 26 million hectares, not 50 million hectares.
problems.correction: 26M hectares of degraded land by 2030 (UNCCD target)
problems.verifierReason: India's UNCCD LDN target is 26 Mha by 2030, announced at COP14 (2019). 50 Mha is incorrect.

problems.quote: Article 356 (during President's Rule in a State)
problems.problem: The power of Parliament to legislate on State subjects during President's Rule is derived from Article 357, not Article 356. Article 356 deals with the proclamation of President's Rule.
problems.correction: Article 357 (during President's Rule in a State)
problems.verifierReason: Article 356 deals with proclamation of President's Rule; Article 357 confers legislative power on Parliament during such Rule.

problems.quote: it has met only 12 times since 1990
problems.problem: As of 2023, the Inter-State Council has met 13 times (the 13th meeting was held in November 2022).
problems.correction: it has met only 13 times since 1990
problems.verifierReason: Inter-State Council held its 13th meeting in Nov 2022; '12 times' was outdated.

problems.quote: The Governor refused to address the Assembly
problems.problem: The Punjab Governor (2021-23) refused to summon the Assembly, not to address it. The constitutional crisis and Supreme Court intervention concerned the summoning of the Assembly.
problems.correction: The Governor refused to summon the Assembly
problems.verifierReason: The 2023 Punjab crisis concerned the Governor's refusal to summon the Assembly, not to address it.

problems.quote: Behram Khurshid Pesikaka v State of Bombay (1955)
problems.problem: Wrong case citation for the proposition that fundamental rights cannot be waived. The leading case is Basheshar Nath v. Commissioner of Income Tax (1959).
problems.correction: Basheshar Nath v. Commissioner of Income Tax (1959)
problems.verifierReason: Original citation wrong; Basheshar Nath (1959) is leading case on non-waiver of fundamental rights.

problems.quote: Independent member joining a party after 6 months
problems.problem: The 10th Schedule disqualifies an independent member if they join any political party after election; there is no 6-month grace period. The 6-month period applies to nominated members.
problems.correction: Independent member joining a party after election
problems.verifierReason: Independent members disqualified on joining party immediately; 6-month grace only for nominated members.

problems.quote: 1/3 of members splitting from party = merger (not defection)
problems.problem: The split provision (1/3) was deleted by the 91st Amendment (2003). Now only merger (2/3) is recognized as an exception to defection.
problems.correction: Merger requires 2/3 members; split provision deleted by 91st Amendment
problems.verifierReason: Split provision (1/3) deleted by 91st Amendment; only merger (2/3) is exception now.

problems.quote: ₹1 granted to regularise expenditure of a service that is now a government responsibility (after the fact)
problems.problem: Token Grant is for a new service not contemplated in the budget, not for regularising past expenditure. Regularisation is done through Excess Grant (Art 115).
problems.correction: ₹1 granted for new service not in budget, pending supplementary demand
problems.verifierReason: Token grant is for new service not in budget; regularisation uses Excess Grant (Art 115).

problems.quote: Art 358 — Art 19 is automatically suspended (for duration of emergency).
problems.problem: After the 44th Amendment, Article 19 is automatically suspended only if the emergency is declared on grounds of war or external aggression, not for armed rebellion. The statement as written is incorrect.
problems.correction: Art 358 — Art 19 is automatically suspended only if emergency is declared on grounds of war/external aggression (not for armed rebellion).
problems.verifierReason: 44th Amendment limits auto-suspension of Art.19 to war/external aggression emergencies.
